analysis:
Examined both inference documentation excerpts and the mlx-swift-lm submodule metadata/pointer change. The complete documentation range map shows that docs/architecture/inference.md:4931–5444 is unchanged surrounding context, not newly introduced media, cache, qualification or lifecycle behavior. It describes authenticated media carriers, tenant-partitioned prefixes and media cache disabling (5017–5019, 5218–5220), bilateral cancellation/retirement (5097–5102), native memory admission (5139–5179), and exclusion of unqualified speculative placements from coordinator pairing (5387). These relate to A-001, T-041, T-010, T-028, T-050 and T-052–T-056, but provide no independently supported regression here.
The actual added documentation at 4816–4826 describes GPT-OSS plain decode command buffers committing every 100 operations without an input-size bound, while prefill keeps MLX defaults. This is scheduling behavior, not evidence of changed encryption, authorization, billing or cache isolation. Its availability, memory-pressure and cancellation implications require implementation verification.
libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 advances the dependency revision, but no dependency source diff is supplied. Therefore no concrete vulnerability can be established or safety concluded. Integration should examine that revision's complete changes, especially GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers and CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding, validating bounded in-flight resource use, cancellation responsiveness and unchanged request arithmetic. The dependency update remains a material coverage limit.
